name: concepts-readroom/a-unread
refs: THE LAYOUT (a flat wireframe, project-owned): where things go on the 1024x600 game screen (the screen is centred in this 16:9 canvas). A dark top bar and a dark bottom line; the wall behind; the table top from a little above the middle down; a brass lamp over the pod; the pod on its dish in the lamp's pool; the creature to its right; small pinned papers top left (a photo and a slip) and top right (a card); dark wooden plates for buttons at the bottom. Take only the placement and the sizes. Never copy its flat look, and paint no lines, arcs or boxes from it.

THE ROOM'S MATERIALS (our signed reading-room bench painting, project-owned): its umber wood, cream plaster wall, the small low brass lamp and its warm pool of light. The new picture is clearly made by the same hand, but at night: the wall goes to soft shadow away from the lamp.

THE POD (project-owned game art): our Loika pod, an upright seed pod with a round coral cap, slate-blue body, pale vertical ribs and coral dots. Keep its shape, cap, ribs and dots; it is the hero of the picture.

THE CREATURE (project-owned game art): the Loika the pod will become: a small round charcoal creature with a cream belly and muzzle, amber eyes, four stubby legs with pale toes and three green leaves on its head. Keep its design exactly; never invent another creature.

THE PAINTED LANGUAGE (one of our signed Vivarium room paintings, project-owned): its matte painterly miniature rendering, soft occlusion, warm golden light, cosy palette. Take the treatment and the warmth only, none of its objects.
prompt:
Paint the WHOLE screen of a cosy handheld creature-keeping game, 16:9, a calm front-on view slightly from above: the READING ROOM, where the player studies a pod (a wild seed pod with a creature's genome sleeping inside it) one page at a time. A naturalist at home after dark, one find on the table.
PLACEMENT (follow the layout): a plain dark slate band (#1d232b) across the very top and one across the very bottom, empty. Between them the wall behind, and a wooden study table whose top runs across the screen from a little above the middle down to the bottom band. A low small brass lamp hangs over the left-centre; its warm pool of light falls on the pod. The POD stands on a low turned wooden dish with a thin brass lip, left of centre, in the pool: the largest, brightest thing on screen. The CREATURE stands on the table to the pod's right, at the pool's edge, about as tall as the pod. Top left, pinned to the wall: a small photo print of the place it was found (a meadow by a pond) on kraft paper with a blank strip under it, and below it a small kraft slip with a tiny painted pod on it (its kin). Top right, pinned: a small cream card with a tiny painting of a Loika with pale patches on its back (the player's goal). At the bottom: one wider dark umber wooden plate with a thin brass hairline centred under the dish (the button), and a row of three smaller plates near the bottom band; all plates BLANK. Leave quiet empty table between the dish and the plate for two short lines of type.
DIRECTION: THE LAMP AND THE GLASS. A dark wooden study table at night under the one low brass lamp; the wall behind is plaster going to shadow, with a window's last deep blue dusk at the far right edge. The pod is lit from above and glows from within like a seed held to a candle. Between its pale ribs its shell is thin warm glass with real depth: a soft rim light on its edges and a faint reflection of the lamp, so what is inside feels truly INSIDE, deep in the glass, not stuck on the surface. The pinned papers are warm kraft with hand-inked edges, small brass pins and a string; one has a pressed leaf. The creature stands at the pool's edge, half in light. The feel: a quiet evening, one find, and something alive in it.
STATE: A POD JUST SET DOWN, FULL OF UNREAD SURPRISES. Inside the pod's glow, deep in the glass, FIVE soft round motes of warm light drift at different depths, each holding a faint pale tiny silhouette of a part of a creature (a lock of fur, an eye, a paw print, a leaf sprig, a curl of tail). The front mote is larger and brighter, with a tiny white four-point spark at its edge (something never seen is here) and a tiny gold pin beside it (the goal may be here). Just under it, two or three tiny faint colour swatches of fur (russet, ash grey, and one left dim and unknown) drift unresolved. The pod is full and alive with promise. The CREATURE beside it is still unread: a soft cool grey fog silhouette of the Loika's exact shape with a thin pale outline, no colour, no face detail, a faint glow on its back where the page in hand belongs; never a guess.
LIGHT AND FINISH: one warm key light from the lamp, warm bounce, soft ambient occlusion, a soft contact shadow under every object. Matte, hand-painted miniature finish like the painted reference, cosy and warm, real depth; low saturation everywhere except the pod's inner light. No gloss, no chrome, no plastic, no neon, no sci-fi interface, no holograms, nothing childish.
NO text, letters, digits, numbers, logos or symbols anywhere (the game types its words later): every paper, card, slip and plate is blank. No frame, no border, no vignette; the screen fills the canvas edge to edge.
